12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is built from the last FILED period only, as the Sector Lead required: the filed H1 2026 sales of Rp535.9bn [S6] carried through a second half at the FY2025 filed H2/H1 seasonality of 1.135x (FY2025 sales Rp979.3bn less H1 2025 Rp458.8bn, all audited [S5]), which gives about Rp1,144bn and 16.8% growth on FY2025A. No line of the un-filed vendor September quarter enters the forecast; the vendor nine-month figure is carried in section 3 as a labelled cross-check that sits within 2% of this build, not as its source [S0]. The growth is mostly price: the deck has Brent at US$96 for FY2026E against US$68.1 in FY2025 [S0], and the link1 pass-through carries about 40% of cost of goods at 95% pass-through. FY2027E falls to 1.0% because that price carry reverses as the deck's Brent steps down to US$84 [S0], leaving volume growth of roughly 4-5% net of a 4pp price give-back; FY2028E-FY2030E return to 3.5-4.5% as the price drag eases (Brent US$80 and US$78) and volume does the work. This is nominal consistency with the deck, not a demand haircut: the underlying volume path is the FY2025 production record and the company's stated share-of-customer strategy [S7, S3].

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Anchored on filed evidence only. The filed H1 2026 interim shows sales of Rp535.9bn and gross profit of Rp79.68bn, a 14.87% margin [S6, F23, F24], against the audited FY2025 margin of 13.96% [S5]. The 15.00% input is the margin before the unpassed-cost link; with the link charging the unpassed share of Brent at the deck's FY2026E US$96 against US$68.1 in FY2025 [S0], it prints a reported FY2026E margin of about 14.3%, i.e. between the audited FY2025 rate and the filed H1 rate. The 0.5pp gap to H1 is the higher full-year input cost, not a haircut: H1 averaged about US$94 and the second half carries the peak. FY2027E is 14.60% input, i.e. about 14.2% reported, as Brent falls to US$84 and the pass-through gives back some of the 2026 price [S0]; the fade then continues to 14.10% by FY2030E with the long-run rate at the FY2025 actual of 13.96% [S5]. We do not annualise the H1 print of 14.87% [S6] and we do not carry the FY2022 9.4% outcome in the base: H1 2026 at Brent near US$94 is the filed evidence that pass-through is working at today's input level [S6, S5, S8]. The red team's FY2022 reconciliation is stated rather than dodged: the same 0.40 x 0.05 link would have charged only about 0.9% of COGS in FY2022 against the 4.6pp margin fall the accounts show, so the link explains a sixth of that episode and the rest was volume loss and price timing. At Brent US$96 the base therefore assumes explicitly that the FY2022 failure does not recur; the FY2022 margin outcome is carried in the bear scenario and in the sensitivity grid, and the judgement rests on the filed H1 print [S6, S8].

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: FY2025 COGS of Rp842.6bn splits into cost of goods manufactured of Rp382.2bn (45.4%) and purchases of finished goods for resale of Rp465.7bn (55.3%) [S5, note 20 p.76]. Inside the manufactured book, raw and indirect materials consumed were Rp339.8bn, 88.9% of manufactured cost and 40.3% of consolidated COGS [S5]. We set the Brent-exposed share at 40% of COGS because it covers the manufactured ink and adhesive book, where petrochemical resins and solvents are the main input [S7]; labour and manufacturing overhead are domestic-cost items [S5]. The traded book is bought and resold at a quoted spread, so its purchase cost and selling price move together and the margin exposure is the spread, not the absolute oil price; we carry that spread risk in the bear rather than in this link.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: High pass-through, but not a flat margin and not complete. Gross margin ran 13.40% in FY2023, 13.40% in FY2024 and 13.96% in FY2025 [S5], yet fell to 9.4% in FY2022 when raw-material prices rose faster than selling prices (F60) [S8]. The 0.95 is the pass-through through a normal input cycle, not through a spike; the 5% left unpassed is the competitive cost of Chinese imports [S3]. H1 2026 at 14.87% with Brent averaging about US$94 [S6] shows pass-through working at today's input level, which is why the base is not set at the FY2022 outcome; the bear carries a partial repeat of that gap.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Audited FY2025 net operating expense is Rp58.60bn, gross profit Rp136.76bn less operating profit Rp78.16bn (F52, F50), i.e. 5.98% of sales [S5]; FY2024 was Rp60.21bn, 6.59% of sales (F53, F51) [S5]. The pack's plug omitted other operating income, so we use the audited net line. FY2026E is the audited Rupiah cost base grown 9%, below the 16.8% revenue growth of this year's filed-basis build, which gives Rp64.1bn and 5.60% of sales: the ratio falls because revenue rises faster than a largely fixed cost base, not because we assume an efficiency gain beyond the company's own FY2025 record of cutting the line in nominal terms (Rp60.21bn to Rp58.60bn) [S5]. From FY2027E, as revenue growth slows to about 1%, the ratio returns to the audited 5.98%.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Restated FY2025 depreciation is Rp7.25bn, 0.74% of sales [S5] (the data pack carries only the Rp3.43bn G&A slice). Capex of Rp1.3bn in FY2025 and Rp2.8bn in H1 2026 is far below depreciation [S5][S6], so the depreciable base and the ratio drift down gently to 0.60% by the terminal year.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Management states no large capex is planned for 2026, only routine operational investment [S3]; nine-month capex to September 2026 was 0.45% of nine-month sales [S0], FY2025 cash capex was Rp1.34bn (0.14% of sales) and FY2024 Rp4.47bn (0.49%) [S5]. We use 0.35% for FY2026E, the run-rate, then 0.30% to FY2028E, and step up to 0.70% by the terminal year so replacement capex converges on the restated depreciation charge of 0.74% of sales [S5] instead of running the asset base down in perpetuity.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Reconciled to the September actual instead of asserted below it. The engine's NWC line matches the pack's net working capital, which was Rp411.4bn at 30 September 2026 [S0]; against our FY2026E revenue build that is 36.0%, and against trailing sales about 36.9%, which is the red team's figure. We hold FY2026E at 35.5%, which is Rp406.2bn: the September actual less the 1.4% seasonal unwind the FY2025 fourth quarter actually shows (Sep-25 NWC Rp310.4bn to Dec-25 Rp306.0bn, a Rp4.4bn release [S0]). So the assumed year-end NWC is Rp406bn against the Rp411bn actual, a Rp5.2bn release, and not the Rp374bn that 32.0% implied. The fade to the audited 31.2% year-end ratio then runs at about 1.2pp a year, reaching it by FY2030E, and is anchored on the two pieces of evidence in the record: receivable days eased from about 121.3 at June to 119.5 at September, and the company collected down to the 31.2% ratio at the FY2025 year-end from a 36.9% September-2025 reading [S0, S6, F67, F54, F56]. A 32.0% FY2026E would have required a Rp37bn fourth-quarter release with no precedent for it. The effect of the change on FY2026E free cash flow and on the target is printed in report section 3.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: FY2025 effective tax was 19.7% of pre-tax profit, H1 2026 20.6% and the nine months to September 2026 20.9% [S5][S6][S0], against the 22% headline corporate rate; we hold 20.5%, the observed rate, with no assumed change in tax law.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 finance costs of Rp3.39bn on opening debt of Rp62.2bn is 5.45%; H1 2026 finance costs of Rp1.48bn on opening debt of Rp51.9bn is 5.70% annualised [S5][S6]. The nine months to September show Rp3.05bn of finance cost already incurred against the FY2025 opening balance of Rp51.9bn, so a 5.70% charge on the opening balance would leave a negative fourth-quarter charge; we use 6.05%, which charges about Rp3.1bn on the FY2026 opening balance and covers the nine-month actual plus a fourth quarter [S6][S0]. This is the effective cost on the opening balance, above the 5.70% H1 rate, because the short-term lines were drawn to Rp110.2bn at June and repaid to about Rp83.5bn at September [S6][S0]. It is consistent with the BI-Rate held at 5.75% in the macro deck plus the ordinary spread.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 finance income of Rp12.20bn on opening cash of Rp240.2bn is 5.08%, after Rp2.03bn of final tax on that income [S5]; H1 2026 finance income of Rp4.04bn on Rp246.8bn is 3.3% annualised because average cash fell [S6], and the nine months to September show Rp5.90bn, a 3.2% realised yield on the opening balance [S0]. We now use 3.2%, the rate the P&L actually earned over nine months, instead of the 4.5% blend that overstated FY2026E finance income against the reported run-rate [S5, S6].

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: No term debt is planned; short-term bank loans fund working capital and are repaid within the year, so net borrowing is set at zero. FY2025 net repayment of Rp12.6bn and H1 2026 drawdown of Rp7.0bn are working-capital swings [S5][S6].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: No recurring non-operating item is disclosed; FY2025 other operating income net of expense was Rp1.1bn and is not forecast to recur [S5].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Minorities took 0.03% of FY2025 net profit; the only subsidiary, PT Colorpak Flexible Indonesia, is almost wholly owned [S5].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The June-2026 AGMS approved a Rp170.51 dividend, 75% of FY2025 net profit, paid on 20 July 2026 inside the September quarter [S4, S5]; the AR policy is a minimum 20% of profit [S7, F43]. Two bases must be kept apart in the report: the CASH paid in FY2026 is the FY2025 declaration (DPS 170.51, Rp52.2bn), while the dividend DECLARED on FY2026E profit is 75% of our forecast, DPS 214.88 and Rp65.8bn, and it is that Rp65.8bn that must be set against FY2026E free cash flow to equity. We use the 75% actually paid, not the 68% three-year average, because the policy floor and the last two distributions both sit at 50-75% and the controlling shareholder takes the dividend [S4].

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Share count is 306,338,500 issued less 298,100 treasury shares; the 2025 buyback was Rp0.3bn and is immaterial [S5]. No rights issue is planned.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Set at the model's own sustainable growth: a 75% payout leaves 25% retention, and on a terminal ROE of about 13% that is 3.25%, i.e. g = ROE x (1 - payout). It is below the house 4.0% ceiling [config] and below the macro deck's long-run IDR inflation, which is appropriate for a mature converter whose terminal value should not assume an ROE above its cost of equity. The DCF's implied P/B is shown in §4 and reconciled to the model's ROE.

challenges.challenge: link1_pass of 0.95 with link1_share of 0.40 charges 0.82% of COGS against a 41% Brent rise (96 vs 68.1). The model's own FY2022 evidence is a 4.6pp gross-margin fall at Brent US$99, when the same formula would have charged only about 0.9% of COGS. FY2026E is therefore a spike-level input year (Brent 96 is +41% on FY2025) priced as a normal cycle, and the only thing separating the two is the nine-month margin print, which is vendor data with no filing. The bear carries the FY2022 outcome but the base pass-through calibration is never reconciled to it.
challenges.answer: The FY2022 reconciliation is now stated in the gross_margin basis and in section 5: the link explains only about a sixth of the 4.6pp fall, so the base explicitly assumes the FY2022 failure does not recur, with the evidence cited as the pack-only nine-month margin and the outcome carried in the bear and the sensitivity grid.

challenges.challenge: The entire Q3 roll rests on S0, the Yahoo Finance pack, with no Q3 interim LK fetched and no fact added: nine-month revenue of Rp849.7bn, gross margin of 14.48%, opex at 5.60% of sales, working capital at 36.9% of trailing sales, September cash of Rp193.2bn and debt of Rp83.5bn are all vendor figures quoted nowhere in fund record (no nine-month or 2026Q3 fact exists) and verifiable against no filing. They drive the FY2026E revenue growth of 19.45%, the gross margin, the NWC input, the bridge and one of the three extreme_call drivers. The report cites [S0] as though it were a filing and nowhere tells the reader the quarter is unaudited vendor data. Under the house rule a load-bearing figure without a citable primary source is FATAL, and this results update adds precisely the unattributable part.
challenges.answer: No nine-month or Q3 interim exists to cite: the company financial-reports page still ends at the June 2026 interim and idx.co.id refuses scripts, checked today. The report now states plainly in the summary and section 3 that every September figure is pack data, and section 4 sizes it: the terminal block is most of the DCF, the FY2026E stub is a fraction of one year, and the grid stays above the price at four points lower growth, so it is a target-precision risk not a rating risk. post_bs_review records the limitation.

challenges.challenge: nwc_pct is lifted from the audited 31.2% (which this reviewer required last round and the analyst accepted) to 34.0% in FY2026E fading to 32.0%, the stated basis being that 'both inventory and receivables' are 'higher again from the June interim' [S0, S6]. The pack shows inventory FELL from Rp250.7bn at June to Rp240.1bn at September (-4.2%) and receivable days fell from about 121.3 to 119.5; the net build is receivables on higher sales plus payables. The step is called 'a permanent capital-intensity step' in the basis and then faded to 32.0% by FY2030E, still above the audited 31.2%, with no source beyond the pack. It costs roughly Rp110-190 a share, 5-9% of the target.
challenges.answer: Basis corrected: the pack shows inventory FELL from Rp250.7bn at June to Rp240.1bn at September, so the build is receivables on higher sales plus payables. nwc_pct is cut from 34.0%/32.0% to 32.0% fading to the audited 31.2% by FY2028E, and the report states the composition and the correction explicitly.

challenges.challenge: The report compares 'the FY2026E dividend of Rp52.2bn' with FY2026E FCFE of Rp0.25bn and FCFF of -Rp6.5bn. Rp52.2bn is the FY2025 declaration (DPS 170.51, paid July 2026 inside the September quarter); the model's FY2026E declared dividend is DPS 214.88, i.e. Rp65.8bn, which is the number it compares with FY2027E FCFE of Rp88.8bn. Section 3 makes it worse by calling the Rp52.2bn 'the distribution out of the larger FY2026 profit, declared on our forecast EPS and paid next year' - it is not. The shortfall against the year's own FCFE is 264x, not 209x, and the amount net cash must fund is Rp65.6bn, not Rp51.9bn.
challenges.answer: The two bases are now separated throughout: cash paid in FY2026 is the FY2025 declaration (Rp52.2bn) while the dividend declared on FY2026E profit is Rp63.7bn, and the cover is struck against the declaration. The section 3 sentence calling Rp52.2bn the distribution out of FY2026 profit is deleted.

challenges.challenge: The FY2026E P&L does not reconcile to the nine-month actuals that now anchor the year. Model interest expense for FY2026E is Rp2.96bn, below the nine-month actual of Rp3.05bn already incurred, which implies a negative Q4 charge. Model interest income is Rp11.47bn against a nine-month actual of Rp5.90bn (run-rate Rp7.87bn), so Q4E carries Rp5.57bn against Q3's Rp1.86bn on lower cash. With Q4 at Q3's interest lines, FY2026E PBT is about Rp105.5bn rather than Rp110.3bn and net profit about Rp83.9bn rather than Rp87.7bn, a 4% cut. Q4E net profit of Rp28.2bn is 12% above Q3's Rp25.1bn while Q4E EBIT of Rp26.4bn is 14% below Q3's Rp30.7bn - the bridge is assumed, not built.
challenges.answer: FY2026E is rebuilt against the nine-month actuals: cost of debt is raised to 6.05% so the opening balance charges about Rp3.1bn, above the nine-month Rp3.05bn, and cash yield is cut to the 3.2% actually earned, taking FY2026E interest income to about Rp8.2bn against the Rp7.87bn run-rate. Net profit falls to Rp84.9bn and the target is re-run on it.

challenges.challenge: The extreme_call BLOCK is cleared by a justification that declines the test: 'The price sits below the value range, so the reverse DCF cannot bracket it.' The flag asks what today's price implies. The justification also says 'revenue passed the board's full-year projection [S0]' when nine-month revenue of Rp849.7bn is 20.6% below the Rp1,070bn plan, and its third driver is a WACC convention (the 5.70% debt cost via coe_premium) rather than an operating driver. With a 48.9% expected return the name needs a defensible reverse DCF, not a table that is above the price in every cell.
challenges.answer: The reverse test is now run rather than declined: the engine returns price not bracketed, so the corners are bracketed by hand and the price requires a WACC above the grid top row with terminal growth below the bottom row, or a permanent FY2022 margin. The plan statement is corrected to a fifth short, and three filing-cited operating drivers are named.

challenges.challenge: The DCF starts from FY2026E and the net-cash bridge is the September 2026 balance sheet, but both multiple legs are struck on FY2025A: 5.25x EBITDA of Rp85.41bn (leg Rp1,824) and 7.03x EPS of Rp222.8 (leg Rp1,566). FY2025A EBITDA is 22.5% below FY2026E and LTM EBITDA is Rp99.67bn, so applying the multiple to the older, lower year is not the 'not capitalising a peak' protection the report claims - it is a horizon mismatch of twelve months inside one valuation. On the pack LTM the EV/EBITDA leg is about Rp2,066 and on FY2026E about Rp2,247; the P/E leg on FY2026E EPS is about Rp2,014. The blend would rise from Rp2,439 to roughly Rp2,612, about Rp170 a share (8%) before the scenario weighting.
challenges.answer: Both bases are now shown and the choice is stated: the peer multiple is trailing so it is applied to FY2025A, but the FY2026E EBITDA and earnings are disclosed alongside, the horizon mismatch is acknowledged, and the legs are read as a floor rather than an estimate because the stale-year basis understates the blend.

challenges.challenge: The net-cash bridge uses Rp109.6bn (September cash of Rp193.2bn less debt of Rp83.5bn) and silently drops Rp19.15bn of marketable securities carried at June (F44, S6); the pack's Q3 investments field is null, so the analyst neither includes nor explains them. Securities are Rp62 a share and the house rule is to value everything the company owns. If they were sold to fund the July dividend the bridge may be right, but the reason is unstated; if they remain, net cash is Rp128.8bn.
challenges.answer: The Rp19.15bn of marketable securities is now in the valuation bridge as a non-operating asset, with the reconciliation stated: the July dividend is funded by the fall in cash, so the securities were not liquidated, and dropping them understated net cash.

challenges.challenge: The market's own discount is never quantified. At Rp1,560 against a probability-weighted Rp2,635, the market implies roughly 41% (about 34% if the price is rolled forward a year at the 11.96% cost of equity), double the house's mechanical 20% liquidity discount and the largest single component of the expected return. The report mentions 'a discount of its own' and stops. Nor is the upside sized: crossing the Rp500m ADTV threshold removes the discount and takes the target to Rp2,635.
challenges.answer: The market-implied discount is now quantified against the house one: at the share price the market discounts the weighted value beyond the mechanical liquidity discount, and closing the gap is worth the whole difference between the published target and the weighted value, with the ADTV threshold case named.

challenges.challenge: The bear shocks revenue -5pp, gross margin -4pp and NWC +3pp, but never touches the payout, although FY2026E FCFE of Rp0.25bn against a declared Rp65.8bn dividend means the whole distribution is funded from the net-cash pile this year and section 5 names a cut as a step-change risk. A payout cut to the 20% policy floor (DPS about 57) would remove about Rp158 a share from the twelve-month return - roughly a third of the 48.9% - and is the most obvious way the scenario set is incomplete.
challenges.answer: The bear now cuts the payout to the twenty-per-cent policy floor alongside the margin, growth and working-capital shocks, because FY2026E FCFE cannot fund a three-quarters distribution; the scenario table shows the bear target and the rating survives it because the bear remains above the price before the discount.

challenges.challenge: The earnings-quality screen stops at FY2025 (accruals -8.3%, +4.0%, -0.4%) and omits the year that changed the picture: nine-month 2026 net profit of Rp59.49bn against operating cash flow of -Rp12.39bn is about 8% of average total assets, roughly 11% annualised - at the house 10% manipulation threshold - with receivables up Rp62bn in nine months and inventory outgrowing COGS. The report classifies the flag as optics without computing the 2026 ratio, and the bear has no impairment or collections case beyond a +3pp working-capital shock.
challenges.answer: The 2026 accruals gap is now computed in section 3 on the same basis as the historical rows and classified optics-class with three sourced reasons, and the bear carries a collections shock and receivable write-down. It is not tabulated as a fact because the nine-month pack figures cannot be registered as S0 facts.

challenges.challenge: The scenarios are mirrored in their drivers but not in value: at equal 25% probabilities the bull adds Rp1,299 a share to the base and the bear removes Rp823, so the probability-weighted value of Rp2,635 sits 4.7% (Rp119) above the base of Rp2,516 - and it is the weighted value, not the base, that is discounted into the published target. The asymmetry is unexplained; the bull's +5pp growth compounds on a higher margin base while its margin shock is smaller (+3pp against -4pp), which double-counts the convexity in the bull's favour.
challenges.answer: The bull margin shock is raised to plus four points, an exact mirror of the bear, and the residual convexity is disclosed with the base-scenario value shown next to the weighted one. The only remaining asymmetry is the bear payout floor, justified in qc_justifications as one-directional and sourced.

challenges.challenge: Two citation and wording defects recur from round 1. The deck's Brent (FY2026E 96, FY2027E 84) is cited to [S3] in three places, and S3 is a Warta Ekonomi news piece with no mention of Brent or oil (source grep returns zero hits). And the summary still says 'the share price is 35.1% below the target' - 1,560 is 26.0% below Rp2,108, and 35.1% is the price upside - which is exactly the wording the round-1 QC note asked to be fixed.
challenges.answer: The deck Brent path is now cited to the pack rather than the news piece in all three places, and the summary wording is corrected to state the target is a percentage above the price rather than the price below the target.

challenges.challenge: The Rp19.1bn marketable-securities bridge item is still in the model and is still a double count; section 4's new defence does not meet the arithmetic. QC Q10 proved the pack cash line is cash plus short-term investments at both filed dates - 31 Dec 2025 254.8388 = 246.7638 + 8.0750 and 30 Jun 2026 240.7906 = 221.6431 + 19.1475 - so the September pack cash of 193.19 already contains the Rp19.1bn, which is also why it fell by about the Rp49.3bn dividend against June. Section 4 answers that "the securities were not liquidated to fund it", which establishes that the securities still exist, not that the cash line excludes them. The item overstates DCF equity by up to Rp19.1bn, about Rp62.6 a share, roughly 2.8% of the target.
challenges.answer: Bridge item deleted. The pack cash field is cash plus short-term investments at both filed dates (254.8388 = 246.7638 + 8.0750 and 240.7906 = 221.6431 + 19.1475), so the September line of 193.19 already contains the securities; net cash is now stated as Rp109.6bn = 193.19 less 83.5 debt. Section 4 reconciles the June cash of 221.6 with the pack aggregate of 240.8 and no longer adds the securities. Target falls.

challenges.challenge: nwc_pct of 32.0% for FY2026E fading to 31.2% is still unreconciled to the September actual. Pack NWC at 30 Sep is Rp411.4bn, 36.9% of trailing sales and 35.2% of FY2026E revenue, so 32.0% implies a Rp37.1bn release in a quarter whose sales rise 2% on Q3, against a seasonal precedent of Rp4.4bn in Q4 2025 and an FY2022 ratio that sat at 36.9%. The stated basis (inventory fell, the build is receivables) explains the composition of the build, not a 5pp fall in the level, and the release is not sized in the report even though it lifts FY2026E free cash flow by the same Rp37bn order.
challenges.answer: FY2026E nwc_pct raised from 32.0% to 35.5%, i.e. Rp406.2bn assumed at the year-end against the September actual of Rp411.4bn: the release is now Rp5.2bn, close to the Rp4.4bn Q4 2025 precedent, not Rp37bn. The fade runs 1.2pp a year to the audited 31.2% by FY2030E. Section 3 prints the assumed NWC against the actual and the effect on FCFF, which goes to negative this year.

challenges.challenge: Section 4 still says the growth-and-margin grid "is struck on the twelve-month value after the liquidity discount, and every cell in it is also above today's price". The engine grid is pre-discount: its centre cell, Rp2,550.05, is exactly tp_base before the 20%. On the stated post-discount basis QC Q13 computed the bottom corner at Rp1,671 and the worst cell at about Rp1,511, below the Rp1,560 price. This sentence is the load-bearing step in the BUY's reverse-DCF argument, and the parallel claim that the engine reports "price not bracketed" because the price sits below the whole grid does not survive the post-discount arithmetic.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now states the growth-and-margin grid is the PRE-discount twelve-month value, with its centre cell equal to tp_base. After the 20% discount every cell but the worst corner stays above the price; the worst corner (growth -4pp, margin -2pp) is a few per cent below it and the next-worst is within a rounding. The claim is corrected to a roughly 2pp sustained margin shortfall, not the FY2022 trough, and qc_justifications.extreme_call is rewritten to the grid actually run.

challenges.challenge: C16 was accepted as FATAL on the requirement to fetch the Q3 2026 interim LK and restate nine-month revenue, gross profit, opex, working capital and September cash and debt as facts, or to hold FY2026E on the last filed basis until the filing arrives. The report now discloses that the Rp849.7bn nine-month sales, the 14.48% margin, the 36.9% NWC and the September cash and debt are vendor pack data with no filing behind them, and then builds FY2026E revenue growth of 19.45% and the 15.0% margin on those very lines. Disclosure is not the resolution the finding required, and this quarter is the reason the target was lifted.
challenges.answer: FY2026E is rebuilt on filed evidence only: filed H1 2026 sales of Rp535.9bn plus a second half at the audited FY2025 H2/H1 ratio, giving Rp1,144.1bn and 16.8% growth. The vendor nine-month figures no longer enter the forecast, only the labelled cross-check in section 3, and the margin is anchored between the audited FY2025 rate and the filed H1 print. A further search on 13 November 2026 found no third-quarter LK or press release carrying the nine-month accounts.

missing_bull_case.note: The largest single upside is mentioned but never sized: at Rp1,560 the market implies a discount of about 34% to the probability-weighted Rp2,635 on a twelve-month-forward basis (1,560 x 1.1196 = 1,747) against the house's mechanical 20%, so the gap between the market's discount and the house rule is worth about a third of the target and appears only as the phrase 'a discount of its own' (C23). Rp19.15bn of marketable securities (F44) sits outside the net-cash bridge (C22). Credit where due: the Q4/Q3 seasonal step used (+2.0%) is below FY2025's (+3.9%), and the FY2026E gross margin of 14.30% after the Brent charge is 0.17pp BELOW the nine-month actual of 14.48%.

missing_bear_case.note: No payout-cut case, although FY2026E FCFE of Rp0.25bn against a declared Rp65.8bn dividend is the whole thesis risk and section 5 names a cut as a step-change risk (C24). No receivable-impairment case, although the 2026 accruals ratio is the largest in the record: nine-month operating cash flow of -Rp12.39bn against net profit of Rp59.49bn is about 8% of average total assets, roughly 11% annualised, at the house manipulation threshold (C25). Supplier interruption (Coim Rp268.5bn, 27% of purchases) is still not a scenario shock.

assumption_realism.note: The revenue path is the strongest part: nine-month sales of Rp849.7bn are 79.4% of the board's Rp1,070bn plan and Q4 needs only Rp220bn to reach it, so the plan was clearly stale and the run-rate re-phasing is right. But the working-capital step rests on a misdescribed build (inventory FELL from Rp250.7bn at June to Rp240.1bn at September) (C17), and the pass-through of 0.95 charges only 0.82% of COGS for a 41% Brent rise, while the same 0.40 x 0.05 link on the FY2022 analogue produces about 0.9% of COGS against the 4.6pp margin fall the accounts show - the link is roughly six times too weak, and the base is defended only by the pack-only nine-month print (C15).

evidence_and_citations.note: A spot-check of the packet facts holds: F26 (Rp1.070bn plan and Rp145bn gross profit) verifies at S7 p.95, and the F23/F24/F37/F41/F71/F72 quotes match. But the nine-month roll has NO fact in fund record at all - nine-month revenue, margin, opex, working capital and the September cash and debt are all [S0] vendor figures with no filing and no quote, and the report does not tell the reader so (C16). The deck's Brent is cited to [S3] in three places and S3 contains no mention of Brent or oil (source grep returns zero hits) (C27).

valuation_method_fit.note: DCF-first with 60/25/15 weights fits a converter, the DCF runs from the September balance sheet with the FY2026 stub only, and the 32% DCF-versus-multiple divergence is disclosed. But the two multiple legs are struck on FY2025A earnings while the DCF starts FY2026E and the bridge is September 2026: FY2025A EBITDA is 22.5% below FY2026E, so the 'not capitalising a peak' defence is inverted and the legs understate the blend by about Rp170 a share (C21). Terminal growth of 3.3% equals the model's own sustainable growth - credit.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose is disciplined and the bear-at-a-discount caveat is stated, but the FY2026E dividend of Rp52.2bn is the PRIOR year's declaration while the model declares Rp65.8bn for FY2026E, so the cover shortfall is understated 1.26x (C18). The extreme_call justification declines the reverse DCF and says revenue 'passed' the plan when nine-month revenue is 20.6% short of it (C20). The summary repeats the round-1 error: 'the share price is 35.1% below the target' - 1,560 is 26.0% below 2,108 (C27). Doubling the bear weight to 40/40/20 still gives Rp1,957 and a 39.2% return, so the rating survives the bias test; credit.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The model reads the right variables consistently: link1 d.oil.brent at FY2026E 96, FY2027E 84 and long-run 75; usd_idr 18,228 spot and 18,350 FY2027E; BI-Rate 5.75 with a 5.70% cost of debt the P&L pays; CHEMICALS template weights 60/25/15. link1_share of 0.40 sits inside the peer range (ADMG 0.05 to 0.72) and the realisation basis (IDR, domestic sales, imported USD-linked inputs) matches the sector deck. The only defect is the citation tag, not the variable (C27).

conservatism_audit.note: Below-last-actual or unsourced drift: nwc_pct raised from the audited 31.2% to 34.0%/32.0% permanently, worth roughly Rp110-190 a share (5-9% of the target), sourced only to the pack and justified by a false statement about inventory (C17); Rp19.15bn of marketable securities omitted from the net-cash bridge (Rp62 a share) (C22); both multiple legs on stale FY2025A earnings (C21). Opposing (optimistic) items: FY2026E interest income of Rp11.47bn against a nine-month run-rate of Rp7.87bn, and FY2026E interest expense of Rp2.96bn BELOW the nine-month actual of Rp3.05bn (C19); FY2026E revenue 9.4% above the board's plan, justified by the run-rate. The directions do not offset and are never shown as a pair.

Three operating drivers, each cited to a filing: (1) the audited FY2025 net opex ratio of 5.98% of sales, taken from gross profit less operating profit, diluted on a larger top line by growing the audited Rupiah cost base 9% [S5, F52]; (2) the audited total FY2025 depreciation charged to operations of Rp7.249bn, of which Rp3.818bn sits in cost of goods manufactured, against the pack's Rp3.43bn general-and-administration-only slice, so the restatement lifts FY2025A EBITDA by Rp3.82bn to Rp85.41bn (EBIT 78.16 + 7.249), and that restated figure is what the model and the multiple run on [S5, F1, F3]; and (3) the net-cash balance of Rp109.6bn at September, being the pack's aggregate cash of Rp193.19bn (cash plus short-term investments, the same line QC proved at both filed dates) less debt of Rp83.5bn; there is no separate securities bridge item because it would double count [S0, S6, F40, F44]. The FY2026E revenue is built from the filed H1 2026 interim and the audited FY2025 halves, not from the un-filed vendor September quarter, which is now only a cross-check [S6, S5]. What the price implies, stated as the engine computes it: the discount-rate grid is all above the price even after the 20% liquidity discount (lowest Rp2,026); the growth-and-margin grid is the PRE-discount twelve-month value, its centre is tp_base, and after the discount all cells but one are above the price - the exception is the worst corner, growth minus 4pp and margin minus 2pp, at Rp1,491, 4.4% below the price, with the next-worst at Rp1,565. So the price implies about a 2pp sustained gross-margin shortfall against base, not a repeat of the FY2022 trough; that is a lower bar than the previous text claimed and it is the honest one. The engine's reverse routine, which solves on revenue growth alone, still returns 'price not bracketed' because even minus 4pp of growth leaves the value above the price.
